device: LG OLED55G29LA, firmware 33.31.61, browser Chrome/120 NetCast SmartTV/10.0 Colt/2.0
method: Local read-only replay using the same anonymized 40-vehicle/105-landmass fixture as PC profiling. 8 HUD players, 10Hz snapshots, zero active weapon projectiles. Render size 1459x1070 or scale=3 at486x356. No production quality defaults changed. Cases were sequential, not randomized.
limitations: Initial tv-replay-baseline ran with screen-off detected and is unsuitable for frame-rate comparison.

Screen power/OS throttling was not continuously observable. Later screenshot may be an OS loading/pause overlay; user reported ship position unconfirmed (expected for replay). Frame cadence must therefore be treated as approximate, not a validated live-play FPS result.
GPU timer query unsupported; timings describe main-thread CPU and driver submission, not GPU execution.
Replay is static and movement acknowledgements are mocked; not a multiplayer input-latency test.
Instrumentation and report collection add overhead; no isolated experiment yet proves the benefit of particular scene optimizations.
findings: Even with zero projectiles, the reduced 486x356/low/no-muzzle-lighting case used about80–86ms of render CPU including logic in the last three sample windows.

In that case active-mesh evaluation took35–39ms, map/radar instruments18–19ms, world visuals10–12ms. These are not all additive: active-mesh evaluation and game logic are already included in total render CPU.
Scene contains3809 meshes in reduced effects mode, versus3875 normally; about175 are active/visible.
A reduced renderer needs object-count/update-cost improvements, not merely disabled muzzle flashes or fewer pixels.
